summary: "Free text dosage" toggle labels are inverted in the drug order form
description:
Repo: openmrs-esm-patient-chart (esm-patient-medications-app)
Steps to reproduce
Open a patient chart with an active visit, then Order basket → Drug orders → Add → search a drug (e.g. Paracetamol 500mg) → Order form.

Look at the Free text dosage toggle while it is switched off (structured Dose / Route / Frequency fields showing).

Switch it on (the free-text dosage box appears).

Actual
Toggle switched off → label reads "On".

Toggle switched on → label reads "Off".

The same inversion appears in translations, e.g. French shows "Activé" while the toggle is off.

Expected
The label matches the toggle state: "Off" when free-text dosage is off, "On" when it is on.
Why it matters
A clinician who believes structured dosing is selected can end up typing into the free-text box instead. Example on test3: Mill QA Test (10003YW), ORD-499 (Zyrtec 10mg) was saved as a free-text order whose only instruction is "-5". It has no dose, route, frequency or duration, so it never expires and stays in Active Medications. In the Edit drug order screen the toggle reads "Off" while the free-text box is visible.
Cause and fix
esm-patient-medications-app/src/add-drug-order/drug-order-form.component.tsx:981-982 passes labelA={t('on', 'On')} and labelB={t('off', 'Off')}. Carbon's Toggle shows labelA when unchecked and labelB when checked (checked ? labelB : labelA), so the labels are swapped.
Fix: labelA={t('off', 'Off')} and labelB={t('on', 'On')}, plus a unit test asserting the label text in both states.
